definition: Posit means to put forward as a claim or possible explanation.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word posit. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know posit should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Rather than blame bad luck, the report posits a simpler cause for the failed harvest: the seed stock itself.
To float an idea is weaker than to posit it — floating just tosses a thought out to see who reacts, with nothing staked on it.
Declare is stronger than posit: a posited claim is offered for testing, while a declared one is announced as settled fact.

To propose is to put a plan before a group so it can be adopted — a route, a budget, a hire. You posit an idea for an argument to examine; you propose an action for people to decide on. Posit hands a claim over for testing, while propose asks for a decision.

To advance a claim is to push it into the discussion with real force behind it — the speaker wants it to win ground. Posit is cooler: a posited claim is laid out for inspection, urged on no one. Advance presses; posit places and steps back.

Where do the bay's young eels come from?

No net had ever caught one being born, so the aquarium's director posited a spawning ground far offshore in the floating weed — a claim she offered to explain the yearly arrivals, and one her critics could now go and test.
Posit is the precise verb because the director put the claim forward for examination, not as settled truth.
Declare would overstate her confidence; posit — literally “to place” — sets an explanation on the table where an argument can inspect it.
Postulate, its cousin on the next card, goes one step further and assumes the claim as a base to build on.
Posit is for essays and seminars: you posit a claim or an explanation so an argument can examine it.
Its neighbors in this unit divide the work — postulate assumes a starting point for reasoning, and surmise draws a hesitant conclusion from scraps.

Something keeps tugging at the outermost objects of the solar system.
Their orbits cluster oddly, tilted the same way, as if herded by a gravity nobody has located.
In 2016 two astronomers posited a ninth planet -- unseen, far beyond Neptune -- as the simplest explanation for the clustering.
They did not claim to have found it.
The paper laid the idea out with its own weak points attached: here is the mass that would do it, here is where it might hide, and here is what would prove us wrong.
A decade of telescope time later, the planet remains an offer on the table -- a candidate explanation, standing exactly where its authors set it, waiting to be confirmed or knocked down.
